title: The Buddha's Story
objective: After this level you can retell the traditional story of Siddhartha Gautama's awakening and say what historians can confirm about him.
summary: Tradition tells how Prince Siddhartha Gautama left home at 29 and awakened at Bodh Gaya. Scholars accept that he lived, though his dates and the details of his life are uncertain.

cards.headline: A prince walked out of his palace at 29 and never went back.
cards.body: That is how Buddhists begin the story of Siddhartha Gautama, the man they call the Buddha. Here is the story as the tradition tells it, and then a harder question: what can historians actually confirm?

cards.headline: The prince and the four sights
cards.body: Buddhist tradition says Siddhartha Gautama was born at Lumbini, in today's southern Nepal, into the Shakya clan. That is why he is often called Shakyamuni, "sage of the Shakyas". He grew up in luxury. Then, the traditional accounts say, he saw four sights: an old man, a sick person, a corpse and a monk. Age, sickness and death come even to princes. At 29 he left his comfortable life behind to look for a way through them.

cards.headline: Six hard years, then one night under a tree
cards.body: For six years he lived as an ascetic, practicing harsh self-denial. Then, Buddhists hold, he sat beneath a pipal tree at Bodh Gaya, in northeastern India, and attained enlightenment. From then on he was the Buddha: an awakened one, who has woken from the sleep of ignorance and been freed from suffering. Tradition says he spent the next 45 years teaching across northeastern India and died at Kushinagar at about 80.

cards.headline: What historians can say
cards.body: Scholars accept that the Buddha lived. But the events in the stories about him can't be taken with confidence as history, and even his dates are uncertain: scholars place his death around 480 BCE or as much as a century later. One early clue is cut in stone. Emperor Ashoka, who ruled from about 273 to 232 BCE, left an inscription recording his visit to the spot he believed was the Buddha's birthplace. Biographies came only centuries later, from around the start of the Common Era.

mascot.line: Two layers, one life: the story believers tell, and the stone historians can date. Keep both, and keep them apart.

cards.headline: The Buddha's Story: the takeaways
learned: Tradition: four sights, six hard years, awakening at Bodh Gaya
Scholars accept he lived; his dates and details are uncertain

questions.explanation: Buddha means an awakened one: someone who has woken from the sleep of ignorance.

questions.prompt: In the traditional story, why did Siddhartha leave his life of luxury at 29?

options.label: He was sent away after his clan lost a war
options.rationale: Tradition gives a different reason: the four sights.

options.label: His father ordered him to study far from home
options.rationale: He left on his own, after the four sights.

options.label: He wanted a new kingdom to rule for himself
options.rationale: He gave up a royal life; he didn't seek one.

options.label: The four sights showed him age, sickness and death

questions.explanation: An old man, a sick person, a corpse and a monk: age, sickness and death come even to princes, so he left to seek a way through them.

questions.prompt: Buddhist teachings were memorized for generations before being written down. Why are historians cautious about details of the Buddha's life?

options.label: The written accounts come long after his death
No inscription mentions his birthplace at all
Buddhists never wrote anything about him
options.rationale: Teachings and biographies were written, just later.

options.label: His dates are known, but his name is not
options.rationale: His dates are the uncertain part.

questions.explanation: The Pali canon was written down only around the 1st century BCE, and biographies came only from around the start of the Common Era, centuries after his death.
